law_name: Tax reform package (six government bills; five passed by the House of Representatives on 22 December 2025)
description: The largest overhaul of the Cypriot tax system since 2002, in force from 1 January 2026: the personal income-tax-free threshold rose from €19,500 to €22,000 (the government had proposed €20,500, the supporting parties DISY, DIKO, DIPA and EDEK obtained more), corporate tax rose from 12.5% to 15% in line with the OECD global minimum tax, the special defence contribution on dividends fell from 17% to 5%, deemed dividend distribution was abolished for post-2026 profits, the defence contribution on rents and most stamp duties were abolished, and an 8% tax was introduced on gains from crypto-assets and approved stock options. It also gave the Tax Commissioner new powers against evasion and made tax returns mandatory for most employed people. Only the capital gains bill passed unanimously; AKEL called the package 'socially unfair, lopsided and incomplete'.
significance: Presented by Christodoulides as 'a fairer, more modern, more competitive tax system' and one of his administration's main policy commitments.

law_name: Law establishing the Deputy Ministry of Migration and International Protection (Υφυπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Διεθνούς Προστασίας)
description: Government bill approved unanimously by the House on 29 February 2024, transferring the interior ministry's migration and asylum departments to a new deputy ministry, the second created by his government after the Deputy Ministry of European Affairs. Nicholas Ioannides became its first deputy minister in 2024. The Cyprus Mail questioned whether a new deputy ministry was needed after a year of falling arrivals.
significance: Centrepiece of the government's migration policy, which it credits with a fall of about 90% in arrivals and a 180% rise in returns compared with 2022.

law_name: Suspension of the examination of asylum applications by Syrian nationals (government decision, April 2024)
description: In April 2024 the government suspended the processing of all asylum applications from Syrians, citing mass arrivals by boat from Lebanon. Human Rights Watch called on Cyprus to resume processing and to stop pushbacks (see polemics).
significance: Part of the migration policy the government credits for lower arrivals; criticised by Human Rights Watch and other rights groups.

law_name: Amalthea initiative: Cyprus maritime corridor for humanitarian aid to Gaza
description: Proposed by Christodoulides in October–November 2023, the mechanism collects, inspects (with Israeli participation) and ships aid from Cyprus to Gaza. It was activated by a joint statement of the European Commission, Cyprus, the UAE, the US, the UK and others on 8 March 2024, and the first ship left Larnaca on 12 March 2024. More than 37,000 tonnes had been delivered by August 2026 according to the foreign ministry, now mostly via the port of Ashdod.
significance: Gave Cyprus a visible role in the Gaza war response; the European Council again backed the corridor in October 2026.

law_name: Cost-of-living allowance (CoLA/ΑΤΑ) agreements between government, unions and employers (May 2023 and November 2025)
description: The interim agreement of 12 May 2023 raised wage indexation from 50% to 66.7% of the consumer price index. The permanent agreement signed on 13 November 2025, after a general strike in September 2025 and a presidential intervention, raises it to 80% (January 2026), 90% (July 2026) and 100% (January 2027), payable in years of real GDP growth with a 4% ceiling, and extends CoLA to more than 55,000 additional workers according to the president.
significance: Ended a long-running labour dispute that had led to nationwide strikes.

law_name: Cost-of-living support packages and minimum wage increase (2023–2024)
description: According to Christodoulides' first-year review, his government adopted support measures worth €196 million (October 2023) and a further €60 million (2024), including longer maternity leave, zero VAT on certain goods, a reduced VAT rate on first homes negotiated with the EU, a 'photovoltaics for all' scheme, and an increase of the national minimum wage to €1,000 a month. It also adopted new rules on hiring advisers to the president and other officials.
significance: The government's main response to post-2022 inflation.

law_name: Cyprus Presidency of the Council of the EU (January–June 2026): main files concluded
description: According to the presidency's own review, presented by Christodoulides to the European Council on 18–19 June 2026: a negotiating framework with figures and partial general approaches on the 2028–2034 MFF; opening of the first cluster of accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova; agreement on the Returns Regulation and entry into application of the Pact on Migration and Asylum; a €90 billion assistance package for Ukraine and the 20th sanctions package against Russia; signature of the EU–Mercosur partnership agreement and agreements with Mexico and Switzerland; the revision of the Air Passenger Rights Regulation after 13 years of negotiation; completion of the Union Customs Code reform; a provisional agreement on the Critical Medicines Act; and an EU summit with regional leaders hosted in Nicosia.
significance: European Council President António Costa described it as highly successful, especially on enlargement; the results listed are the presidency's self-assessment.
